candidates.name: Indus Appstore

deferral.reason: A channel to EVALUATE, not one to ship: [ADR 076]'s rider names the Indus Appstore for its 0% commission on in-app payments. No developer account exists, so no row is written to the channel register and no submitter is built; the facts below are read first.
ownerSteps: open an Indus Appstore developer account, as the entity the other Android channel uses — the account kind is what an entity change later has to move
read the developer terms and record the commission as a tooling/catalog/fee-register.json cell, with the date read and its URL
then scaffold the channel: node tooling/kit/new-channel.mjs --id indus-appstore --dry-run, and --write once the row's facts are read

commission.verify: UNREAD: the 0% figure is the rider's, not a reading of the store's terms. Read the Indus Appstore developer terms and write the cell with asOf before any margin is computed from it.

candidates.exportDuty: The same as android-play once built: the listing is ours (rendered from app.yaml), the reviews and ratings stay with the store, and the package name is permanent — so it must be the SAME package id the Play channel ships.

_why: EVERY STORE CHANNEL IS A REGISTER ROW PLUS A SUBMITTER THAT PASSES ONE DRY-RUN CONTRACT. The row is tooling/channel-register.json's (cited by `channel`, never restated); the submitter is the ChannelSubmitter each script exports (tooling/release/submit-common.mjs): validate · plan · upload · status. Adding a store is a row, an adapter here, and a submitter that passes submitterConformance — tooling/kit/new-channel.mjs scaffolds the three.

One adapter per `kind: store` row, and the contract test holds that set equal both ways. The web row and the two `kind: direct` rows have no store to submit to and no adapter. `vendor` is null on every adapter on purpose: the store is the row's, and apple-app-store, google-play and microsoft-store stay placed once in _non-port.json as billing authorities.

L2, not L3, CLAIMED: every adapter is chosen per call by its channel id and passes the conformance suite DRY, against recorded fixtures with no network. No channel is served and no `upload` has ever run here, so nothing has shown the upload half conforms; the claim waits for a first real submission on two channels.
apps-gov-in is `external`: the portal has no submission API (the row's noSubmissionApi), so its path is a person at the portal and there is nothing to call dry or wet.

cost.feeCells is the STORE's commission where the store bills: Play Billing and Apple IAP. The paddle-rail stores take none on our own checkout; that rail's cells are the payments port's. secrets are none here: every store credential is named once in the register's signing.ciSecrets and ciSecretRegister.
candidates holds a store not built because an owner step stands first. Its commission is UNREAD until the store's terms are read and dated.
